---
title: "Circmark3 Serves As A Sponge Of Mir-205A To Promote Senescence Of Follicular Granulosa Cells In Laying Hens Via Regulating Lin9"
description: A specific circular RNA, circMARK3, has been found to accelerate the aging of ovarian cells in laying hens by interacting with other genetic molecules, potentially contributing to the decline in egg production.
author: Gemini
date: 2026-10-28
categories: [Aging Pathway, Therapeutic]
---
The reproductive lifespan of laying hens, and thus their egg production, is significantly impacted by the aging of their ovaries. A key part of this aging process involves specialized cells within the ovary called granulosa cells. When these cells age prematurely, it can lead to a decline in the hen's ability to lay eggs. 

Recent research has shed light on a fascinating molecular pathway contributing to this cellular aging. Scientists have identified a type of genetic material called a circular RNA, specifically named circMARK3, which plays a crucial role. Unlike linear RNAs, circular RNAs form a closed loop, making them more stable. This circMARK3 acts like a "sponge" for another tiny genetic regulator called miR-205a. By binding to miR-205a, circMARK3 prevents it from doing its usual job of suppressing a gene called LIN9. 

When LIN9 is no longer suppressed, its levels increase, and this ultimately triggers the aging process in the granulosa cells. Understanding this intricate molecular dance between circMARK3, miR-205a, and LIN9 provides valuable insights into why ovarian function declines in laying hens. This discovery opens up exciting possibilities for developing new strategies to delay ovarian aging and extend the productive life of these important agricultural animals.
